competitors.name: White Rabbit
competitors.action: White Rabbit secured an ASDA rollout for three gluten-free frozen sourdough SKUs across 522 stores starting May 11, while Morrisons simultaneously broadened the brand's range into 605 stores. That is a strong distribution signal inside a niche Real Dough should watch closely: premium, better-tasting frozen pizza with a clearly differentiated dietary promise.

competitors.name: Loopini
competitors.action: Loopini is now showing as a new frozen pizza brand at Target with at least two premium SKUs live on the retailer site, a useful signal that Target is still willing to add higher-priced, differentiated frozen pizza concepts rather than only scaling incumbent mass brands.

competitors.name: ZeroCarb LYFE
competitors.action: ZeroCarb LYFE is pushing a different kind of frozen pizza expansion: protein-led, zero-carb comfort food backed by $8 million in institutional funding, a community Wefunder raise, and active sell-through goals at Target. Even if the concept is far from Real Dough's lane, it is another sign buyers are opening freezer space for sharply positioned nutritional propositions.

trends.topic: Frozen pizza shelf growth is favoring sharply framed niche propositions over generic premium claims
trends.magnitude: Today's clearest signals were gluten-free sourdough national distribution at White Rabbit, premium better-for-you Target shelf placement for Loopini, and macro-driven functional positioning from ZeroCarb LYFE.
trends.context: For Real Dough, the implication is pretty direct: buyers still want differentiation, but it has to be legible fast. 'Sourdough' alone is not enough unless it is paired with a crisp retail promise around taste, process, or nutrition that stands apart from adjacent niche brands.

breaking.headline: The freezer aisle is still making room for niche pizza brands when the proposition is instantly understandable
breaking.impact: White Rabbit is scaling gluten-free sourdough through mainstream grocery, while Loopini and ZeroCarb LYFE show Target is willing to support both premium indulgence and functional nutrition stories. Real Dough should keep tightening the one-line buyer story around authentic sourdough quality and why it deserves shelf space versus these increasingly specific competitors.
